name: School
spec: fluorescent yellow-green pentagon (pointed top) with two black children walking
meaning: You are near a school; watch for children and obey the school speed limit.

snippets.back: Unless another limit is posted or lawfully established, the favorable-condition maximum in a school zone is twenty miles per hour.
Pavement messages such as SCHOOL ZONE or RR CROSSING are painted in white letters on the road to warn of conditions ahead.
A permanent five-sided, pentagon-shaped school crossing sign warns that children may be crossing at any time of day.

Obey red-and-white orders like DO NOT ENTER, retreat from WRONG WAY signs, red night reflectors confirming; yellow-black circles and Xes mark rail crossings, pentagons schools, diamonds dangers, rectangles rules.
Take extra care near school buses in neighborhoods and school zones, where students board, leave and cross the road.
The handbook lists fifteen miles per hour in District alleys and school zones unless otherwise posted.
Watch especially carefully for children near schools and homes, and do not speed in school zones.
Speeding draws three points to fifteen over, four past sixteen, and six in a crash, scene-leaving over fifty dollars draws six, and texting draws three plus three in school zones or six in a crash.

result.summary: Pentagon school-crossing shape and warn-for-children meaning confirmed by official snippets; school-zone caution/speed action consistent.
